terms.meaning: A trick where a file name like dot-dot-slash tries to escape a folder and read other files.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports
sections.what: Brings in the file system and path tools, and sets the Node.js runtime.
sections.why: Needed to find and read the file.

sections.name: ALLOWED_EXT
sections.title: Allowed file types
sections.what: Lists the only file types this route will read: markdown and plain text.
sections.watch_out: Adding a type here exposes those files to anyone who can reach this route.

sections.name: GET
sections.title: Read a persona file
sections.what: Checks the file name is safe and allowed, confirms the path stays inside the persona folder, then returns the file content.
sections.why: Stops anyone reading files outside the persona folder.
sections.watch_out: The folder check is a simple prefix comparison. It is safe only because dot-dot names are rejected before it runs.

summary: Reads one persona notes file (markdown or plain text) from the persona folder and returns its contents.
purpose: Gives the app access to the user's written persona notes.
why: Likely reason: keeps longer notes out of the code.
how: Checks the file name is safe, the type is allowed, and the resolved path stays inside the persona folder. Then checks the file exists, reads it, and returns the content.
inputs: A file query parameter in the URL.
outputs: The file name and its content, or an error with status 400, 404, or 500.
risks: No login check is in this file. If the app has no other guard, anyone who can reach the URL can read these notes. The path checks look sound.
debug: 404 means the file is not in the persona folder. 400 means the path or the file type was rejected.
